intro: A histogram cannot reveal the original positions within a bin. Rebinning therefore requires an explicit within-bin model; this exercise uses constant density.
task: Redistribute piecewise-uniform bin mass according to interval overlaps between two edge grids.
requirements: Both edge vectors are strictly increasing with gaps at least 1e-6. masses is nonnegative with one entry per old bin and positive total; it need not sum to one.
The new edge range must cover the entire old edge range. Assume uniform density within each OLD bin.
Return masses on the new bins by distributing each old mass in proportion to interval overlap. Preserve total mass.

Unless a requirement explicitly sets another range, numeric inputs are real and finite with magnitude at most 10000. Booleans are rejected except explicit boolean masks. Vectors have length 1..64 and matrix axes 1..64 unless specified otherwise. Leave inputs unchanged. Raise ValueError for invalid types, bounds, shapes or documented domain conditions.

hints.title: Choose the representation
hints.body: Compute the intersection length between each old interval and each new interval.

hints.title: Build the result
hints.body: Divide each intersection by the old interval width before multiplying by its mass.

explanation: A histogram cannot reveal the original positions within a bin. Rebinning therefore requires an explicit within-bin model; this exercise uses constant density.

Each old bin distributes all of its mass across the covering new grid. Mass conservation is essential, but rebinning and then reversing the operation may lose detail because the intermediate uniformity assumption changes.
